source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"No emotional impact, since the diagnosis is purely medical in nature","B":"A single, uniform emotional response identical for every client","C":"Shock, fear, anger, or grief, among other responses, which can vary significantly between individuals and change over time","D":"Responses that remain completely static throughout the entire cancer experience"}}
source_row.rationale: Clients newly diagnosed with cancer may experience a wide range of psychological responses, including shock, fear, anger, or grief, among others, which can vary significantly between individuals and change over time as they process and adjust to the diagnosis, warranting individualized nursing support.
source_row.source_detail: Range of Psychological Responses to Cancer Diagnosis
source_row.source_name: ONS — Psychosocial Response to Cancer Diagnosis
